reviewerNotes: I agree with the writer's flag. The restaurant and clerks notes both cite cl 24.4(d). claims: Part-time employees are paid 265% because their 15% part-time allowance applies too (cl 10.2).
whys: The Cleaning Services Award extra 15% for part-time employees looks like a loading, not an allowance. The term and the clause number (10.2) should be checked against the award. The string has a hyphen, so the checker locks it in this pass.

The site's own constants call this a 'part-time loading' (calc-boiler/lib/constants/modern-awards.ts:77, partTimeLoading). The note calls it an 'allowance', so the site uses two different terms for one entitlement.
reviewerNotes: I agree with the writer's flag. The cleaning note calls the 15% a part-time 'allowance', but modern-awards.ts:77 calls the same cl 10.2 15% a 'part-time loading'. The term should be checked against the award. The string has a hyphen, so it is locked and was not edited.

claims: Two awards on this site work the other way: Manufacturing and Nurses express the casual rate as a percentage of the casual hourly rate
whys: award-rates.ts NOTES gives Mining the same structure ('Casual rate is 250% of the casual hourly rate (Schedule B.2.3), which is 312.5% of the minimum rate'), and MINING_AWARD in lib/constants/modern-awards-oct2.ts (around line 1086) has casualPenaltyBasis: "compounded". Other awards also have compounded bases (modern-awards.ts lines 822 and 1223, modern-awards-oct2.ts lines 577 and 738, modern-awards-oct.ts lines 754 and 762). The hard-coded count 'Two' and the names 'Manufacturing and Nurses' look stale. The sentence should be generated from PUBLIC_HOLIDAY_AWARD_RATES.filter(r => r.casualCompounded).

lib/data/public-holidays/award-rates.ts line 87 NOTES.mining says the Mining casual rate is 250% of the casual hourly rate (312.5% of the minimum rate), so Mining is compounded too. casualCompounded is computed per award in fromModernAward (line 101), so the count and the names should come from PUBLIC_HOLIDAY_AWARD_RATES.filter(r => r.casualCompounded).
reviewerNotes: I confirmed the writer's fact question. The answer hard-codes 'Two awards ... Manufacturing and Nurses' as the compounded casual awards. In award-rates.ts, NOTES.mining (line 87) describes Mining the same way (250% of the casual hourly rate), and fromModernAward derives casualCompounded per award, so the count and the names may be stale. The text is unchanged and the question goes to the owner.
